name: GynRepanel
description: GynRepanel is a statistically-rigorous negative-result calibration benchmark integrating multi-omics (transcriptome, methylome, proteome, copy-number) for three gynecologic malignancies: high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (OV/ HGSOC), endometrial carcinoma (EC/EEEC), and cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CESC), across TCGA, CPTAC, and PRIDE PXD046507 cohorts. Three A-level frozen findings with dual-independent-toolchain confirmation (Level 4 IJGC 2024 retrospective evidence only): Negative Marginal Value: Adding extra omics layers strictly reduces cross-cohort transfer ARI from 0.282 (transcriptome-only) to 0.194 (full 4-omic, Domain A monotone ↓; Domain B 0.312 → 0.193 ↓). Undecidable Classification: Top-1 (KMeans ARI=0.3947) vs Top-2 (Co-assoc ARI=0.3760) methods achieve pairwise Holm-corrected p=1.000 across 28 tests; champion label flips 50% across held-out cohorts; TOST N3/N4/N5 strata all reject the inequality-null and are declared equivalent within a clinically meaningless bound. Covariance Fragility: Batch × platform double perturbation inflates the between-omic covariance (λ2) standard error by 82.5%, while the marginal ΔARI < 0.01 signal remains reproducibly stable — the limiting factor for subtyping is not sample size but spectral equivalence (λ2) and over-constrained cross-omic covariance structure.
